answer: To secure the consensus protocol against Sybil domination, validators must deposit collateral that faces quadratic slashing penalties upon any detected double-signing event. This architecture creates a steep economic ledge, where malicious collusion risks total erosion of assets. This capital barrier acts as a protective reef, forcing attack costs to scale super-linearly as a vast river of liquidity absorbs honest-state validation. Thus, the marginal cost of coordinating discrete nodes guarantees a negative expected utility, preserving a robust Nash equilibrium.
